newsitem.title: FRANCE: France starts 1997 with new jobless rise.
newsitem.headline: France starts 1997 with new jobless rise.

text.p: French unemployment rose by 18,100 in January, leaving the rate of people out of work at a record 12.7 percent, the labour ministry said on Friday.
The number of people registered without work rose 0.6 percent to 3,099,800 after dipping slightly the month before, the ministry said.

The jobless rate based on International Labour Organisation standards remained at its peak of 12.7 percent, where it has stood since last November although there was some relief from the problem of youth unemployment.
The number of men under 25 seeking jobs fell 1.5 percent while the number of women fell 0.7 percent, the ministry said.

French Prime Minister Alain Juppe gathered students, business and union leaders earlier this month to try to find a way to curb 25 percent youth unemployment, a key issue ahead of next year's parliamentary elections.

Despite plunging popularity and demands that the government give more priority to unemployment, Juppe and President Jacques Chirac are sticking to budget cuts and austerity plans designed to allow France to join a single European currency in 1999.
